items.title: Winard Harper interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 10, 2014
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] The Joe Wilders of the world. [INTERVIEWEE] Right. It’s like polished.

ctx.x: that I was close with or I worked with were. A lot of times they may not have worn it on their sleeves, but if you got to know them, okay, how they conducted themselves, you knew that there was something underlying in there that was intact. You know, Billy Taylor, Max Roach, Billy Higgins, Jackie McLean, Abdullah Ibrahim. All those guys that I spent time with that had a big influence on me, you know Betty, you knew that there was some things intact. And it had to be for them to be the kind of people that they…
The Joe Wilders of the world.

Right. It’s like polished. As far as you know, they might not have had two nickels. You know what I mean? But you know they were still dignified. It was something in their intent. It was something that they were trying to say. It was a message in all of it.
